title: WPSS/2414/2024 of KHUSHBU Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
2024:UHC:9973
I N THE HI GH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAI NI TAL
HON'BLE JUSTI CE SRI RAKESH THAPLI YAL
December 27, 2024
W r it Pet it ion ( S/ S) No. 2 4 1 4 of 2 0 2 4
Khushbu .......Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ......Respondents

Counsel for the Petitioner: Ms. Gurbani Singh and Ms.
Sukhwani Singh, learned
counsel.
Counsel for the respondents: Mr. Jayvardhan Kandpal, Brief
Holder.
Counsel for the respondents: Mr. Kishore Rai, learned
counsel holding brief of Mr.
Parikshit Saini, learned counsel
for respondent nos.4 and 5.
Upon h ear in g t h e lear n ed Cou n sel, t h e Cou r t m ade t h e f ollow in g Or der :
1. Petitioner is a married daughter of the deceased
em ployee, the father of the petitioner, who died in
harness, who is aggrieved by rejecting her claim for
com passionate appointm ent.
2. Petitioner being dependent and m arried daughter
of deceased em ployee subm itted representation seeking
com passionate appointm ent, however claim of the
petitioner has been rejected on the ground that as per
the Governm ent Order dated 21.11.1995 m arried
daughters are not included as a m em ber of the fam ily
of deceased em ployee.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner subm its that the
reasons, as given in the order im pugned, rejecting the
claim of the petitioner for com passionate appointment,
cannot sustain in view of the judgm ent passed by the
Full Bench of this Court in Special Appeal No.187 of
2017 Udham Singh Nagar District Co-operative Bank
Ltd. and Another vs. Anjula Singh and Others decided
1

2024:UHC:9973
on 25.03.2019. The issue cam e up before the Full
Bench of this Court, in view of the reference made by
the Division Bench of this Court by the order dated
05.02.2018 passed in Special Appeal No.187 of 2017
and the following questions were fram ed to be
answered by the Full Bench: -
"(i) Whether any of the members, referred to in the
definition of a "fam ily" in Rule 2(c) of the Uttar Pradesh
Recruitment of Dependants of Government Servants
Dying in Harness Rules, 1974 (for short "the 1974
Rules") and in the note below Regulation 104 of the U.R.
Co-operative Committee Employees Service Regulations,
1975 (for short "the 1975 Regulations") would be entitled
for compassionate appointment even if they were not
dependent o the Government servant at the time of his
death?
(ii) Whether non-inclusion of a "married daughter" in
the definition of "family", under Rule 2(c) of the 1974
Rules, and in the note below Regulation 104 of the 1975
Regulations, is discriminatory, and is in violation of
Articles 14, 15 and 16 in Part HI of the Constitution of
I ndia?"
4. These questions have been answered in para 64 of
the Full Bench judgm ent, which are being extracted
hereunder: -
"i. Question No.1 should be answered in the
affirmative. I t is only a dependant member of the family,
of the Government servant who died in harness, who is
entitled to be considered for appointment, on
compassionate grounds, both under the 1974 Rules and
the 1975 Regulations.
ii. Question No.2 should also be answered in the
affirmative. Non-inclusion of "a married daughter" in the
definition of a "family", under Rule 2(c) of the 1974 Rules
and the note below Regulation 104 of the 1975
Regulations, thereby denying her the opportunity of
being considered for compassionate appointment, even
though she was dependent on the Government servant
at the time of his death, is discriminatory and is in
violation of Article 14, 15 and 16 in Part I I I of the
Constitution of I ndia.
iii. We, however, read down the definition of "family",
in Rule 2(c) of the 1974 Rules and the note below
Regulation 104 of the 1975 Regulations, to save it from
being held unconstitutional. As a result a "married
daughter" shall also be held to fall within the inclusive
2

2024:UHC:9973
definition of the "family" of the deceased Government
servant, for the purpose of being provided
compassionate appointment under the 1974 Rules and
the 1975 Regulations."
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner subm its that
since by virtue of the judgm ent rendered by the Full
Bench of this Court, the married daughters are also
included as m ember of the deceased and dependent-em ployee, therefore, she is entitled to get appointm ent
on com passionate ground.
6. Mr. Jayvardhan Kandpal, learned Brief Holder
subm its that U.P. Recruitm ent of Dependents of
Governm ent Servants Dying in Harness Rules, 1974 (for
short the 1974 Rules) are not applicable to the aided
institutions and since the respondents' institution is an
aided institution, therefore, the procedure, as laid down
in the Governm ent Order dated 21.11.1995, annexure 9
to the writ petition, which was adopted on 10.07.2021,
are applicable.
7. Mr. Jayvardhan Kandpal subm its that in view of
Clause 2 of this Governm ent Order since petitioner
being a m arried daughter, is not included as m em ber of
the deceased family, therefore, she is not entitled to get
com passionate appointm ent.
8. Be that as it may. If we go through with the
provision of the 1974 Rules, particularly the definition of
the fam ily the sam e is alm ost identical to Clause 2 of
the Governm ent Order dated 21.11.1995, which was
adopted by the State in the year 2021. Since questions,
3

2024:UHC:9973
as fram ed by the Division Bench of this Court in its
order dated 05.02.2018 passed in Special Appeal
No.187 of 2017, have been answered by the Full Bench
of this Court in affirm ative that the married daughters
are included as a m em ber of the deceased fam ily,
therefore, the argum ent, as advanced by Mr.
Jayvardhan Kandpal are not acceptable.
9. Mr. Jayvardhan Kandpal also fairly subm its that in
Clause 2 of the Governm ent Order dated 21.11.1995,
the definition of fam ily are identical to the definition of
fam ily as defined in 1974 Rules and have also not
disputed this fact that married daughters are included
as a m em ber of the deceased fam ily, have also been
answered by the Full Bench of this Court in affirm ative.
10. Mr. Kishore Rai, learned counsel holding brief of
Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel for respondent nos.4
& 5 also subm its that petitioner being a m arried
daughter is the m em ber of the deceased fam ily in view
of the judgm ent of the Full Bench of this Court,
therefore, her claim was wrongly rejected.
11. After hearing the subm issions as advanced by
learned counsel for the parties further after gone
through with the judgm ent rendered by the Full Bench
of this Court dated 25.03.2019 in Special Appeal
No.187 of 2017, and also after exam ining Clause 2 of
the Governm ent Order dated 21.11.1995 and the
definition of fam ily, as defined under Section 2(c) of the
1974 Rules, this Court is of the view that the petitioner
being a m arried daughter of the deceased em ployee is
4

2024:UHC:9973
the m em ber of the deceased fam ily, therefore, the
rejection of her claim for com passionate appointment
cannot sustain.
12. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed. The
im pugned orders are quashed. The respondents are
directed to consider the claim of the petitioner for
com passionate appointm ent afresh in the light of the
judgm ent rendered by the Full Bench of this Court in
Special Appeal No.187 of 2017 decided on 25.03.2019,
by a speaking and reasoned order, preferably within a
period of two months from the date of production of
certified copy of this order.

RAKESH THAPLI YAL, J.
